title: GOV-0033: build badf-requirements authoring skill — salvage PR #47 onto the canonical G02 gate (supersedes #47)
problem:
## Observed

`main` (`a20df5e`) has **no `skills/badf-requirements/` directory** — there is no authoring skill for G02 requirement decomposition, even though the canonical G02 gate (`BADF-WP-0041`/PR #71) already enforces the four artifacts (`requirements`, `nfr`, `traceability`, `definition-of-ready`). PR #47 proposed such a skill but is **superseded and non-mergeable**: it duplicated the G02 gate as a standalone `scripts/badf_requirements.py` + a custom `schemas/requirements-rtm.schema.json`, re-used the already-occupied `WP-2026-0028` / `BADF-DEM-0015` identities, and rewrote the lockfile against ancient `main`. Its Actions run fails. Issue #46 (which #47 claimed) is already closed as completed. **#47 must not be repaired or merged in place.**

But #47's **authoring layer is still valuable**: the RTM decomposition model, the quantified-NFR discipline, the security-provenance rule, and the authority boundary "author requirements, never approve G02".

## Expected

Build **badf-requirements** as a top-level **authoring** skill (sibling of `badf-prd`), salvaging only the authoring layer onto the **canonical** G02 gate — the same pattern by which `badf-prd` salvaged external methodology from PR #44. Land at **`IMPLEMENTED`**; do **not** advance to VALIDATED/ACTIVE (a separate WP validates it with cases A/B/C).

Keep: `skills/badf-requirements/SKILL.md` + `references/requirements-decomposition.md` + `references/methodology-provenance.md`; register `IMPLEMENTED`; `tests/test_badf_requirements_skill.py`.

Do NOT port: `scripts/badf_requirements.py`, `schemas/requirements-rtm.schema.json`, `templates/requirements-rtm.json`, the old `WP-2026-0028` / `BADF-DEM-0015` / old lockfile, or any duplicate G02 gate logic. **`badf_gate.py` remains the sole G02 enforcement authority.**

The skill authors toward the canonical artifacts and validates with `python3 scripts/badf_gate.py dossier <g02-dossier>` (like `badf-prd`). It declares the invariants **REQ-I01 (no gate authority)** … **REQ-I06 (security provenance)**. The rich `OBJ→CAP→EPIC→REQ→NFR→AC→TEST→EVDREQ` chain is retained as the **authoring model**; the gate consumes only its **canonical subset** (capability/epic/test-obligation/evidence-obligation are NOT made first-class gate objects — no schema growth by speculation; a later failing-first WP adds them only if real project use proves the need).

## Evidence

- Canonical G02 (measured): `requirements` (unique `REQ`, each → ≥1 objective), `nfr` (quantified target), `traceability` (bidirectional complete RTM), `definition-of-ready` (human sign-off covering the exit criteria). Leaner than #47's graph by design (PR #71 deferred the capability/epic hierarchy).
- `badf-prd` is the template: an authoring skill, `IMPLEMENTED`, no validator of its own, salvaged provenance in `references/`.

## Unknowns

Whether capability/epic/test-obligation ever need first-class gate enforcement — deferred to a future failing-first WP, not decided here.
